cases.title: Design a Distributed Unique ID Generator
cases.subtitle: Generate 64-bit strictly monotonic, roughly time-ordered IDs at 100,000+ QPS without central coordination bottlenecks.
functional: IDs must be globally unique 64-bit integers fitting standard database primary keys.
IDs must be roughly sortable by generation time (enabling index locality).
System must generate over 100,000 unique IDs per second with < 2ms latency.
nonFunctional: High availability (99.999% uptime) with zero single point of failure (SPOF).
Clock drift resilience (safe handling of NTP backward time jumps).
deepDives: Twitter Snowflake bit allocation: 1 sign bit + 41-bit millisecond timestamp + 10-bit machine/datacenter ID + 12-bit per-millisecond sequence counter (4,096 IDs/ms per node).
Addressing NTP backward clock drift: If `current_timestamp < last_timestamp`, pause thread until clock catches up or fail over to backup logical sequences.
commonMistakes: Using UUIDv4 (128-bit, non-sequential, severely degrades B-tree index insertion performance).
Using auto-incrementing SQL ID with step offsets (creates tight database coupling and cross-datacenter sync delays).
cases.seniorNotes: At senior staff level, discuss how Snowflake IDs encode the node ID, which could leak datacenter topology or generate rate patterns if exposed raw in client-facing URLs. Mask with Feistel cipher or format-preserving encryption if exposed.

cases.title: Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor
cases.subtitle: Enable multi-user simultaneous document editing with sub-100ms sync and conflict-free convergence.
functional: Multiple authors can edit the same document concurrently in real-time.
Offline editing mode with automatic reconciliation upon network reconnection.
Cursor position and selection presence broadcast to all active collaborators.
nonFunctional: Strong Eventual Consistency (SEC): All connected peers converge to the exact same text without central locking.
deepDives: Operational Transformation (OT) vs Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDT): OT requires a central transformation server (e.g. Google Docs). State-based and operation-based CRDTs (e.g. Yjs, Automerge using RGA trees) allow decentralized peer convergence without central mediation.
Websocket gateway connection tier with Redis Pub/Sub room clustering for broadcast.
commonMistakes: Relying on last-write-wins (LWW) timestamp registers for character streams, which leads to character clipping and lost edits.
cases.seniorNotes: Emphasize garbage collection of deleted character tombstones in CRDT data structures to prevent unbounded memory growth over prolonged collaborative sessions.

cases.title: Design a Global Distributed Rate Limiting Service
cases.subtitle: Enforce per-tenant throughput budgets across distributed API gateways with minimal latency overhead.
functional: Enforce rate limits based on client IP, authenticated User ID, or API Key.
Support multi-tier limits (e.g. 100 req/sec and 50,000 req/day).
Return remaining quota and retry-after headers on HTTP 429.
nonFunctional: Evaluation overhead < 2ms at P99 so upstream API latency is unaffected.
Soft-fail behavior: If rate limiting cluster becomes unreachable, fail open to avoid blackholing traffic.
deepDives: Local gateway token caching with batch synchronization to central Redis cluster to reduce remote round trips.
Sliding window counter algorithm using Redis sorted sets (ZSET) vs Lua script atomic hash maps.
commonMistakes: Executing naive `GET` then `SET` in Redis, causing critical race conditions under concurrent client bursts.
cases.seniorNotes: Address cross-region rate synchronization latency: rather than synchronizing every single token across oceanic links, partition the global quota across regions proportionally to historical regional traffic.

cases.title: Design a Global URL Shortener (TinyURL)
cases.subtitle: Convert billions of long URLs into compact 7-character aliases with sub-10ms redirection and 100:1 read-to-write scale.
functional: Given a long URL, generate a compact 7-character alias.
When a user accesses the short link, redirect to the original destination.
Support optional custom alias names and expiration dates (default 5 years).
nonFunctional: High availability: 99.99% uptime with read requests unaffected by write outages.
deepDives: Base62 encoding of 64-bit distributed IDs avoids hash collisions and costly database existence queries.
Caching the top 20% most active links in Redis satisfies 99% of read requests directly from RAM.
commonMistakes: Using MD5 truncated hashes, leading to collisions that force serial retry queries.
Using 301 redirects when click analytics and tracking are required.
cases.seniorNotes: At senior staff level, discuss multi-region replication. Deploy Redis read-replicas in regional edge datacenters; short URL reads are served locally while writes synchronize asynchronously via Kafka.

cases.title: Design a Real-Time Scalable Chat Application (WhatsApp/Slack)
cases.subtitle: Support 50M+ concurrent WebSocket connections with end-to-end encryption, 1-on-1 and group messaging, and presence.
functional: Support 1-on-1 and group chat rooms with real-time text delivery.
Provide message state tracking: Sent, Delivered, and Read receipts.
Track real-time online/offline presence status.
nonFunctional: Zero lost messages with offline storage and push notification fallback.
deepDives: Stateless WebSocket gateways paired with Redis session registries mapping user_id to active gateway server.
Wide-column message storage (Cassandra/ScyllaDB) partitioned by conversation_id with clustering on message timestamp.
commonMistakes: Maintaining stateful session data on gateway nodes without a distributed registry, preventing horizontal failover.
Using HTTP short polling instead of persistent WebSocket bi-directional streams.
cases.seniorNotes: For massive group chats (10,000+ members), fan-out on write into 10,000 queues exhausts memory. Transition to fan-out on read with cursors, where clients pull from the channel log upon opening.

cases.title: Design a Scalable News Feed & Timeline (Twitter/Instagram)
cases.subtitle: Generate personalized timelines for hundreds of millions of users balancing extreme celebrity fan-out with instant scrolling.
functional: Users can publish posts (text, images) to their followers.
Users view an aggregated chronological and ranked timeline of followee posts.
Support pagination and real-time feed updates.
nonFunctional: High availability with eventual consistency for new posts.
deepDives: Hybrid fan-out: push (fan-out on write) for regular users (<25k followers); pull (fan-out on read) for celebrities to avoid write amplification.
Redis Sorted Sets (ZSET) caching the top 800 post IDs with epoch timestamps as scores.
commonMistakes: Pushing celebrity posts to 80 million follower caches on write, causing catastrophic worker queue collapse.
Executing complex multi-table SQL joins at read time across 500 followees.
cases.seniorNotes: Address inactive users: do not precompute timeline caches for users who have not logged in for 14 days. Reconstruct their timeline on demand upon login to save petabytes of Redis RAM.

cases.title: Design an E-Commerce Flash-Sale Order Pipeline
cases.subtitle: Handle flash-sale surges with 100,000+ concurrent checkout requests without overselling inventory.
functional: Users place orders with items reserved temporarily during checkout.
Process payments securely and release expired inventory reservations.
Enforce zero overselling of limited-stock items.
nonFunctional: Strict consistency for item inventory counters.
Checkout throughput > 20,000 orders/sec during surge events.
deepDives: Atomic inventory decrement in single-threaded Redis via Lua scripts, bypassing relational database row locks.
Saga Orchestration pattern coordinating Order, Payment, and Inventory services with automated compensating transactions.
commonMistakes: Using standard relational SQL transactions with row locks, freezing database connection pools under concurrent load.
Failing to implement compensating inventory restoration on payment failure.
cases.seniorNotes: Implement virtual waiting rooms (token bucket admission) at the CDN edge so excess flash traffic is metered into checkout queues rather than collapsing backend services.

cases.title: Design a Geospatial Ride Matching & Dispatch Platform (Uber)
cases.subtitle: Process real-time driver GPS telemetry and match riders with optimal nearby drivers with sub-second response times.
functional: Drivers stream location pings every 4 seconds.
Riders request a ride and view estimated pickup time (ETA) and fare.
System dispatches the optimal nearby driver in real time.
deepDives: Hierarchical hexagonal spatial indexing (Uber H3) enables O(1) adjacent cell lookups without trigonometric spherical distance scans.
Bipartite batch matching: aggregating ride requests over 5-second windows to optimize global driver-rider travel time.
commonMistakes: Querying SQL database tables using Haversine formula on raw (lat, lon) coordinates on every query.
Matching riders greedily to the nearest driver, creating starvation in congested city centers.
cases.seniorNotes: Discuss dynamic surge pricing: compute real-time demand-to-supply ratio per H3 hexagonal cell and smooth multipliers across neighboring cells using Gaussian blur to avoid pricing cliffs across street corners.
